snakes.common_name: Barred coral snake
snakes.description: Slender elapid with black body and red/white bands, distinctive eye stripe
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic)
snakes.behavior: Secretive, burrowing, avoids confrontation, bites only when provoked
snakes.habitat: Lowland moist forests, gardens, low hills, burrowing in leaf litter
snakes.diet: Small burrowing snakes (worm snakes, blind snakes)
snakes.venom_toxicity: MODERATE RISK - Neurotoxic (affects nervous system, respiratory difficulties). Rare human contact.

snakes.common_name: Boie's keelback, Northern water snake
snakes.description: Slender, semi-aquatic snake with varied coloration (green, red, orange, white, black markings)
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (Catanduanes, Polillo, Calayan, Luzon)
snakes.behavior: Secretive, semi-aquatic, defensive when approached
snakes.habitat: Near water sources, streams, wetland areas, farmland
snakes.diet: Fish, frogs, invertebrates
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Hemotoxic via nuchal glands (limited human risk)

snakes.common_name: Dog-toothed cat snake, Large blunt-headed tree snake
snakes.description: Large snake over 2m, orange-brown with white-edged dark bars, enlarged front teeth, vertical pupil 'cat eyes'
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia and Philippines (Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Indonesia)
snakes.behavior: Arboreal, nocturnal, defensive, ambush predator
snakes.habitat: Lowland and secondary forests, forest edge, adapted to disturbed habitats
snakes.diet: Birds, eggs, lizards, bats; pursues prey using jaws and tail
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Neurotoxic (rear-fanged); potent but effects reversible with neostigmine

snakes.common_name: Gervais' worm snake, Philippine dwarf snake
snakes.description: Small fossorial snake, max 25.5 cm total length; brown-black with pale underbelly
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Basilan, Catanduanes, Cebu, Mindanao, Mindoro, Negros, Panay, Luzon
snakes.behavior: Fossorial (burrowing), rarely seen, cryptic
snakes.habitat: Forest litter, plantations, under stones, between tree buttresses; near sea level to 1000m elevation
snakes.diet: Earthworms, small invertebrates
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Günther's Philippine shrub snake, Banded Philippine burrowing snake
snakes.description: Small burrowing snake endemic to Philippines
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Luzon, Mindoro, Cebu, Negros, Panay
snakes.behavior: Secretive, non-aggressive, burrowing
snakes.habitat: Forest habitat, burrows
snakes.diet: Small prey, burrowing animals
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: King cobra
snakes.description: World's longest venomous snake; average 3.18-4m, record 5.85m; diverse coloration from black with stripes to brown-grey
snakes.geographic_range: Indian Subcontinent through Southeast Asia to southern China (widespread)
snakes.behavior: Solitary, daytime hunter, can expand distinctive hood, produces deep resonant hiss, protects eggs
snakes.habitat: Forests, fields, villages, water-adjacent areas
snakes.diet: Preys almost exclusively on other snakes; dominant predators are humans
snakes.reproduction: Oviparous; only ophidian building above-ground egg nest, female protects throughout incubation
snakes.venom_toxicity: EXTREME RISK - Neurotoxic (primary neurotoxins target respiratory centers). Single bite delivers enough venom for 20 humans/elephant. Causes respiratory failure, cardiac arrest.

snakes.common_name: Luzon dwarf snake, Philippine dwarf snake
snakes.description: Small fossorial snake; characterized by 2-6 dark crossbands behind head
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Luzon and Panay
snakes.behavior: Fossorial, cryptic, rarely encountered
snakes.habitat: Forest floor, burrowing
snakes.diet: Small invertebrates, earthworms
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Mangrove snake, Gold-ringed cat snake
snakes.description: One of largest cat snakes, averaging 8-9 feet (2.4-2.7m); slender black with narrow yellow bands around face and body
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia (Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Indonesia)
snakes.behavior: Nocturnal, arboreal, spends days coiled in mangrove branches near rivers/coastal waters
snakes.habitat: Riverine mangrove forests, coastal mangrove swamps, overhanging waters
snakes.diet: Birds (primary prey - venom effective on avian muscle), rodents, lizards, bird eggs
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Mildly venomous (denmotoxin); can cause painful swelling/discoloration but not lethal to humans

snakes.common_name: Müller's wolf snake
snakes.description: Non-venomous colubrid with divided nasals, transverse light bands on body and tail
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (Batan, Luzon, Mindoro, Polillo)
snakes.behavior: Secretive, terrestrial
snakes.habitat: Forest floor, leaf litter
snakes.diet: Small vertebrates, insects
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: North Philippine temple pit viper, Bornean keeled green pit viper, Banded keel-throated pit viper
snakes.description: Bright green with thin crossbands in blue, red, or white; females larger (96cm) than males (46cm); juveniles/males red-dotted, females blue or red
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia (Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines including Cebu, Luzon, Panay, Leyte, Samar, Palawan)
snakes.behavior: Arboreal with prehensile tail, vegetation dweller up to 20m height
snakes.habitat: Lowland rainforests, low vegetation
snakes.diet: Birds, small mammals, frogs
snakes.venom_toxicity: MODERATE RISK - Neurotoxic and hemotoxic (predominantly neurotoxic with hemotoxic component). Localized effects, rarely systemic, not known fatal.

snakes.common_name: Northern short-headed snake
snakes.description: Small colubrid endemic to Philippines
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Mindoro and Luzon; possibly Sumatra (contested)
snakes.behavior: Terrestrial, secretive
snakes.habitat: Coastal forests, mid-montane tropical forests, secondary growth; sea level to 600m elevation
snakes.diet: Small prey, eggs
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Paradise tree snake, Paradise flying snake, Garden flying snake
snakes.description: Slender body with dark-edged yellow scales creating flower-petal patterns; red/orange/yellow coloring on dorsal surface; green specimens without bright markings also exist
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia and beyond (Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, Brunei, India-Andaman, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore)
snakes.behavior: Diurnal, arboreal, excellent climber favoring coconut palms; remarkable gliding ability (10m+ distances) via rib flaring and serpentine motion
snakes.habitat: Moist forests, plantations, villages, rural gardens, coconut groves
snakes.diet: Tree-dwelling lizards, bats
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Mildly venomous, rear-fanged; can also constrict prey

snakes.common_name: Philippine blunt-headed cat snake, Leyte cat snake, Philippine blunt-headed tree snake
snakes.description: Short blunt brown head distinct from neck, very large eyes with vertical pupils, slender laterally compressed body, light brown with dark transverse blotches
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Bohol, Catanduanes, Leyte, Luzon, Mindanao, Negros, Polillo, Samar, Panay, Romblon, Tablas
snakes.behavior: Fully arboreal, ambush predator
snakes.habitat: Lowland and montane tropical moist forests, disturbed habitats
snakes.diet: Birds, eggs, flying lizards, geckoes
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Mildly venomous (rear-fanged)

snakes.common_name: Philippine bronzeback treesnake, Philippines bronzeback, Striped bronzeback
snakes.description: Arboreal colubrid with distinctive coloration
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic and Micronesia-Saipan)
snakes.behavior: Fully arboreal, fast-moving
snakes.habitat: Trees, arboreal habitats
snakes.diet: Lizards, small prey
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Philippine cat snake, Tawny cat-eyed snake
snakes.description: Very slender up to 213cm (7ft); big head with large cat-like elliptical pupils, white chin extending to half-body, tan/light brown/coffee/pale orange body
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Luzon, Camiguin Norte, Babuyan Claro, Dalupiri; 50-800m elevation
snakes.behavior: Highly nocturnal, nervous when alarmed, strikes repeatedly when defensive, raises head and expands neck scales
snakes.habitat: Pristine and disturbed old-growth tropical forests, secondary forest, forest edge
snakes.diet: Voracious hunter - primarily birds and fledglings, near chicken coops, may enter homes, frogs, lizards, rodents
snakes.reproduction: Mating November-January; females lay 6-14 eggs in tree trunk holes; males slender with bright coloration; females stouter/duller
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Mildly venomous (slightly stronger than most Boiga); rounded mouth unlikely to cause envenomation

snakes.common_name: Philippine cobra, Northern Philippine cobra
snakes.description: Stocky, highly venomous spitting cobra; called 'ulupong' in Tagalog
snakes.geographic_range: Northern Philippines (Luzon, Mindoro, Catanduanes, Masbate)
snakes.behavior: Solitary, mainly terrestrial, nocturnal, ambush predator; extremely fast and agile; rise upwards and produce hood when threatened; spit venom to 3m
snakes.habitat: Lowland habitats, burrows, rocks, rice fields
snakes.diet: Small mammals (rats/mice primary), frogs, other snakes, eggs, birds
snakes.reproduction: Breed year-round; females lay 10-20 eggs; hatchlings independent when hatched
snakes.venom_toxicity: EXTREME RISK - Neurotoxic postsynaptic (one of most toxic Naja venoms). Pure neurotoxin, no necrotizing components. Murine LD50 0.18 mg/kg. Minimal local signs; complete respiratory failure in <30 minutes possible.

snakes.common_name: Philippine pit viper
snakes.description: Highly venomous pitviper with specific scalation patterns
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Agutayan, Batan, Camiguin, Catanduanes, Dinagat, Jolo, Leyte, Luzon, Mindanao, Mindoro, Negros, Panay, Polillo
snakes.behavior: Arboreal, often perching on branches; proficient ambush predator; can descend to ground hunting frogs; nocturnal; typically not aggressive but defends when cornered
snakes.habitat: Lowland moist forests, forest edges, plantations
snakes.diet: Small mammals, lizards, frogs, birds
snakes.venom_toxicity: EXTREME RISK - One of world's most venomous snakes with no specific antivenom yet available

snakes.common_name: Philippine stripe-lipped snake, Philippine cylindrical snake
snakes.description: Small colubrid endemic to Philippines
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Luzon and Polillo
snakes.behavior: Secretive, rarely encountered
snakes.habitat: Forest habitats
snakes.diet: Small prey
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Philippine whipsnake, Keel-bellied whipsnake
snakes.description: 3-6 feet long; dark brown/black with light green/pale blue flecks, bright red tongue, cream lateral stripes bisected by dark lines
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines (endemic) - Luzon (Bataan), Mindoro, Sibuyan, Panay, eastern Mindanao (Diuata Range)
snakes.behavior: Cathemeral (day/night active); docile but nervous; springs up to flee or remains motionless; expands neck showing coloration; moves in sidewinding manner
snakes.habitat: Primary and secondary lowland tropical forests, forest floor among leaf litter
snakes.diet: Specialized hunter - primarily geckos and lizards; may also eat frogs, fish, slugs
snakes.reproduction: Parthenogenic (rare in snakes - majority females). Mating November-January; 2-6 eggs per clutch; sperm storage reported
snakes.venom_toxicity: MILD RISK - Mildly venomous (rear-fanged); small mouth unlikely to cause problems; no fatalities reported

snakes.common_name: Red-tailed green rat snake, Arboreal ratsnake, Red-tailed racer
snakes.description: Bright/light green or gray morph (Panay, Philippines); red/brown tail; dark horizontal eye line; black tongue with brown/blue sides; head yellow-green/green/yellow
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, India-Andamans, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Philippines)
snakes.behavior: Arboreal, spends life in trees/cavities, seldom descends; inflates neck when stressed; unpredictable temperament, may strike or bite
snakes.habitat: Trees, tree cavities, arboreal life
snakes.diet: Birds, lizards, bats, frogs, arboreal rodents, bird eggs
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous

snakes.common_name: Reddish rat snake, Philippine rat snake
snakes.description: Long slender snake up to 1.7m; brownish-red coloration; reddish tail; faint eye-to-jaw stripe; light bands on juveniles fade with age
snakes.geographic_range: Philippines
snakes.behavior: Move around daytime but active nighttime; lifts front body S-shape when threatened; defensive display to scare; bites only if too close
snakes.habitat: Forest edges, near fields/farmland, tree holes, ground holes, caves, abandoned buildings
snakes.diet: Rats, mice (primary), lizards, small birds; hunts by smell following scent trails; kills by constriction
snakes.venom_toxicity: NONE - Non-venomous; kills prey by constriction

snakes.description: Small, slender ground-dweller averaging 40 cm (max ~48 cm); gray-brown back with faint dark lines, yellowish or white belly with black blotches, and tiny white dots along the belly sides.
snakes.geographic_range: Endemic to the Philippines—Babuyan Islands, Luzon, Mindoro, Polillo, Negros, Cebu, Panay and others.
snakes.behavior: Secretive, ground-dwelling, often found under logs, debris, or in ant nests or leaf litter.
snakes.habitat: Forest floor, under logs, debris piles, forested lowlands and foothills.
snakes.diet: Feeds on smaller snakes (especially Pseudorabdion, Calamaria), lizards, and reptile eggs.
snakes.reproduction: Oviparous, breeds during the rainy season (Dec–Mar); lays 5–6 eggs under logs/ant hills.
snakes.venom_toxicity: None—non-venomous and harmless to humans.

snakes.description: The world’s longest snake—recorded over 10 meters (32.8 ft). Most adults are 3–6 m (10–19 ft). Pattern: complex of black, yellow, white and gold on grey/tan, ‘reticulated’ net-like design.
snakes.geographic_range: Southeast Asia (Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines).
snakes.behavior: Excellent swimmer, can colonize remote islands; nocturnal, often active at night.
snakes.habitat: Tropical forest, woodland edge, grassland, near rivers and lakes; also found in disturbed areas.
snakes.diet: Mammals (rats, monkeys, deer, pigs), birds, sometimes large prey (occasionally recorded to have preyed on humans and crocodiles).
snakes.reproduction: Oviparous; females lay 15–80 eggs (typical 25–50); female broods and incubates.
snakes.venom_toxicity: None—non-venomous constrictor; subdues prey by constriction.
snakes.lifespan: Approximately 20–25 years in the wild; up to 30+ years in captivity.
snakes.conservation_status: Least Concern (IUCN); hunted for skin, meat, and pet trade in some regions.

snakes.description: Long, slender body (up to ~2 m); olive-brown with smooth, glossy dorsal midline scales (not keeled like some other rat snakes); 14–15 dorsal scale rows anteriorly.
snakes.geographic_range: Endemic to the Philippines (Luzon, Polillo, Catanduanes, Leyte, Panay, Negros).
snakes.behavior: Diurnal, active on the forest floor by day; climbs at night; alert and fast-moving.
snakes.habitat: Lowland and montane tropical forests, often near streams or damp vegetation; wide habitat tolerance.
snakes.diet: Primarily rats and other rodents, small vertebrates.
snakes.reproduction: Oviparous; lays eggs in moist safe hiding places.
snakes.venom_toxicity: None—non-venomous and harmless to humans.
snakes.conservation_status: Least Concern (IUCN); listed among ‘Other Threatened Species’ in the Philippines due to persecution.
